name: reply.intent
description: Classify a reply to a RIG cold email and route it: positives go to a human, stop-requests suppress the contact. Input is the reply text plus the subject line it answered.

intent.instructions: What does this reply actually say, choosing the single best match

criteria.interested: Interested in the offer or asks for more detail, pricing, or a call but not yet a specific time
criteria.meeting_request: Proposes or asks for a specific meeting time, or accepts a proposed time
criteria.not_now: Interested in principle but timing is wrong -- 'circle back next quarter', 'swamped until March'
criteria.not_interested: Declines the offer outright: 'not interested', 'not a fit', 'no thanks', 'we already have this covered'
criteria.referral: Hands RIG to someone else: names a colleague, forwards it, or says 'talk to X'
criteria.out_of_office: Automated vacation or absence notice with no human answer in it
criteria.unsubscribe: Asks to be removed, unsubscribed, or to stop all contact
criteria.bounce: A delivery failure or mailer-daemon notice -- the message never reached a person

asks_to_stop.instructions: The reply asks RIG to stop, remove, or unsubscribe the contact in ANY wording -- 'please remove me', 'take me off your list', 'stop emailing', 'not interested, do not contact again', or an unsubscribe instruction.

unsolicited_pitch.instructions: This reply is itself a sales pitch, an agency solicitation, or a vendor offer TO RIG rather than an answer to RIG's outreach.

ambiguous.instructions: The reply is too short or too unclear to classify with confidence -- for example a one-word answer, a forwarded thread with no comment, or text in a language the classifier cannot place.

rules.reason: the contact asked to stop -- suppress all further sends and log the suppression
declined -- no further sends to this contact
hard bounce -- suppress the address and clean the list before any further send
positive reply -- a human writes the answer, not the sequence
meeting request -- a human books it and owns the thread
referral -- a human follows the introduction
inbound vendor pitch -- route it to the vendor rule, never back into a reply sequence
reply does not classify cleanly -- a human reads it
classifier is split between intents -- a human reads it

notes.routing: ESCALATE is a handoff to Mike, never an auto-reply. BLOCK means the sequence must not send to this contact again. not_now and out_of_office are the only intents that pass clean: both mean 'queue, do not reply now'.
notes.thresholds: Provisional and uncalibrated; BLOCK rules report ESCALATE with a downgraded-BLOCK reason until calibrated (law 3).
